exposure: Emergency cesarean delivery for non-reassuring fetal heart rate
Active phase of labor vs. non-laboring
Active labor group vs. non-labor group
cohort: Pregnancies necessitating emergency cesarean delivery for non-reassuring fetal heart rate between January 2009 and December 2013
finding: Emergency cesarean delivery for non-reassuring fetal heart rate performed before active labor is associated with a higher rate of pregnancy complications, abnormal cord insertion, smaller placentas, and worse neonatal outcome compared to those performed during active labor.
mod_finding: Emergent cesarean deliveries for non-reassuring-fetal-heart-rate performed before active labor were associated with a higher rate of pregnancy complications, abnormal cord insertion, smaller placentas, and worse neonatal outcomes.
